raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Adds opt-in `KernelConfig.w4a16_prefill_dequant` (`off`/`soft`/`hard`, default `off`). When it is enabled, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` caches a dense fp16/bf16 copy of each weight at load time and runs GEMMs with `M >= 256` on it, so prefill no longer dequantizes int4.

## Claims

- TTFT −22% to −26% on Qwen3-4B/8B w4a16 and −21% on Gemma-4-31B AWQ with MTP-3, on Strix
  Halo (gfx1151). TPOT is unchanged at concurrency 1.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K is within ±0.6 pp.
- Decode, small batches and spec-decode verify stay on the int4 path.
- Default `off` leaves current behaviour unchanged.

## Validation

Usage: `--kernel-config '{"w4a16_prefill_dequant": "hard"}'`. `vllm bench serve` with random 2048 in, concurrency 1, `off` vs `hard` on the same build, interleaved (3 pairs per Qwen model, 2 for Gemma); values are the mean of per-run medians. Measured only on gfx1151; the kernel also runs on other gfx11/gfx12 parts, where the `M >= 256` threshold may need tuning.

| Model | TTFT off → hard | TPOT off → hard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, fp16 (asym) | 1328 → 1033 ms (**−22.2%**) | 27.7 → 27.7 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, bf16 (asym) | 1341 → 1023 ms (**−23.7%**) | 28.2 → 28.2 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-4B w4a16, fp16 (sym) | 782 → 578 ms (**−26.1%**) | 16.4 → 16.5 ms |
| cyankiwi Gemma-4-31B AWQ, MTP-3, 128 out | 8.75 → 6.88 s (**−21.4%**) | 68.0 → 67.2 ms |

`off` matches current main (554340f3d3) within 1% TTFT on all four models.

At concurrency 16 (Qwen3-8B fp16, 512 in / 256 out, 64 prompts, 2 pairs): TTFT 3069 → 2252 ms (−26.6%), TPOT 85.2 → 83.1 ms.

GSM8K (in-tree `tests/evals/gsm8k`, 5-shot, 500 questions, concurrency 16), Qwen3-8B: fp16 0.886 → 0.880, bf16 0.872 → 0.878.

`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`: All 191 passed on gfx1151.

## Details

- **Why opt-in:** the copy is 4x the int4 layer weight and is taken from the `gpu_memory_utilization` budget, so it comes out of KV cache. Qwen3-8B: +13.5 GiB weights, −13.5 GiB KV. Gemma-4-31B: weights 20.2 → 75.1 GiB, KV 71.6 → 16.6 GiB. The trade targets unified-memory parts like Strix Halo, where TTFT matters more than KV capacity. A copy is taken only while the budget still leaves 4 GiB of activation headroom plus KV cache for one `max_model_len` request; past that, `soft` keeps the layer on int4 and `hard` raises.
- **Why `M >= 256`:** below it the dense GEMM is still memory bound and reads 4x the bytes. Per-GEMM on gfx1151 it is up to 2.3x slower than int4 on Gemma-4-31B MLP shapes. At 256 and above it is no slower on any Qwen3-8B or Gemma-4-31B shape measured.

### Related Work
- no open PR caches a dense copy of W4A16 weights for this kernel.
- #55711 makes the int4 prefill dequant cheaper, and this PR skips it, so the two stack. On top of #55711 this PR still cut TTFT by 6.7% (Qwen3-8B fp16), 12.8% (Qwen3-4B fp16) and 23.0% (Qwen3-8B bf16, since #55711 is fp16 only)
- #52637 (int4 repack in `process_weights_after_loading`) and #55742 (profiler labels) touch the same file, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
- #53709 applies the same idea (opt-in load-time dequant for prefill) to DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on another GPU family. It's a different kernel with no shared code path.

How does this test that memory bound batches stay on int4? It seems to only assert the accuracy of the computed solution
Please also mention the advantage of doing this

We pad fp16 weights in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55090 for improved performance.
Can we got through UnquantizedLinearMethod to benefit from that automatically here too once #55090 is merged?

Good point. I routed the cached dense copy through `UnquantizedLinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` at load time and the dense prefill GEMM goes through `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`. Once #55090 is merged, the copy gets the gfx11 row-stride padding with no further change here.

Fair point. It only checked this implicitly: the dense copy was all zeros, so taking the dense path would have produced a mismatch, but the test didn't make that clear. I've replaced it with a dispatch test that swaps in fakes for the HIP skinny, Triton and dense GEMMs and asserts which one runs.

+def _build_prefill_dequant_case(K: int, N: int, G: int, has_zp: bool):
+    """Return (layer, kernel, w_int4_nk, scales_nkg, zp_nkg) for a CT layer."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mixed_precision.MPLinearKernel import (
+        MPLinearLayerConfig,
+    )
+    from vllm.scalar_type import scalar_types
+
+    w_int4_kn = torch.randint(0, 16, (K, N), device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    scales_nkg = 0.05 * torch.rand((N, K // G), device=device, dtype=torch.float16)
+    if has_zp:
+        zeros_int4_gn = torch.randint(
+            0, 16, (K // G, N), device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        zeros_ckpt = _pack_int4_along_n_for_zp(zeros_int4_gn).t().contiguous()
+        zp_nkg = zeros_int4_gn.t().contiguous()
+    else:
+        zeros_ckpt = zp_nkg = None
+
+    layer = _build_dummy_layer(
+        _pack_int4_along_k_to_ckpt(w_int4_kn), scales_nkg, zeros_ckpt
+    )
+    config = MPLinearLayerConfig(
+        full_weight_shape=(K, N),
+        partition_weight_shape=(K, N),
+        weight_type=scalar_types.uint4 if has_zp else scalar_types.uint4b8,
+        act_type=torch.float16,
+        group_size=G,
+        zero_points=has_zp,
+    )
+    kernel = RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel(
+        config,
+        w_q_param_name="weight_packed",
+        w_s_param_name="weight_scale",
+        w_zp_param_name="weight_zero_point" if has_zp else None,
+    )
+    return layer, kernel, w_int4_kn.t().contiguous(), scales_nkg, zp_nkg
+
+
+def _prefill_dequant_vllm_config(mode: str, gpu_memory_utilization: float):
+    from vllm.config import CacheConfig, KernelConfig, VllmConfig
+
+    return VllmConfig(
+        kernel_config=KernelConfig(w4a16_prefill_dequant=mode),
+        cache_config=CacheConfig(gpu_memory_utilization=gpu_memory_utilization),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_zp", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["off", "soft", "hard"])
+def test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant_cached(mode, has_zp, dist_init):

+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA/HIP device not available")
+
+    from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    K, N, G = 256, 128, 128
+    layer, kernel, w_int4_nk, scales_nkg, zp_nkg = _build_prefill_dequant_case(
+        K, N, G, has_zp
+    )
+
+    # Utilization 1.0 leaves all free memory in budget, so the tiny layer fits.
+    with set_current_vllm_config(_prefill_dequant_vllm_config(mode, 1.0)):
+        kernel.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+    if mode == "off":
+        assert not hasattr(layer, _W_DEQUANT_ATTR)
+        return
+
+    expected = _dequant_reference(w_int4_nk, scales_nkg, zp_nkg, G).to(torch.float16)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        getattr(layer, _W_DEQUANT_ATTR), expected, rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+    assert _W_DEQUANT_ATTR not in layer.state_dict()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["soft", "hard"])
+def test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant_budget_exhausted(

+    """Over budget, soft keeps the int4 prefill path and hard raises."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA/HIP device not available")
+
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+
+    # The real free memory is machine dependent; 40 GiB free with 50 GiB
+    # outside a 0.5 budget leaves nothing to spend.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        hybrid_module,
+        "MemorySnapshot",
+        lambda device: SimpleNamespace(
+            free_memory=40 * 2**30, total_memory=100 * 2**30

+    set_random_seed(0)
+    layer, kernel, *_ = _build_prefill_dequant_case(256, 128, 128, has_zp=False)

+    with set_current_vllm_config(_prefill_dequant_vllm_config(mode, 0.5)):
+        if mode == "hard":

+        else:

+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("min_kv_gib, cached", [(0, True), (8, False)])
+def test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant_reserves_min_kv(
+    min_kv_gib, cached, dist_init, monkeypatch
+):
+    """The budget keeps room for one max_model_len request of KV cache."""
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA/HIP device not available")
+

inline_comments.body: How does this test that memory bound batches stay on int4? It seems to only assert the accuracy of the computed solution
Please also mention the advantage of doing this

We pad fp16 weights in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55090 for improved performance.
Can we got through UnquantizedLinearMethod to benefit from that automatically here too once #55090 is merged?

Good point. I routed the cached dense copy through `UnquantizedLinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` at load time and the dense prefill GEMM goes through `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`. Once #55090 is merged, the copy gets the gfx11 row-stride padding with no further change here.

Fair point. It only checked this implicitly: the dense copy was all zeros, so taking the dense path would have produced a mismatch, but the test didn't make that clear. I've replaced it with a dispatch test that swaps in fakes for the HIP skinny, Triton and dense GEMMs and asserts which one runs.
